chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan, from his father, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Al-Fazl! Is there any place for you whereby you can sit in and do business with the people?' I said, 'Yes'.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is none from a Believing man who goes or comes to his gathering or his marketplace, so he is saying when he places his foot in the marketplace, "O Allah! I ask You from its goodness and the goodness of its people", except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would allocate with him one (Angel) who would protect him, and guard him until he returns to his house.'

So he (the Angel) would be saying to him: 'I have rescued you from its evil and the evil of its people on this day of yours by the Permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and I have graced its goodness and the goodness of its people to you in this day of yours'.
So when he sits in his seat, he says when he sits,

"I testify that there is no god except for Allah, One, not having any associates for Him, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Rasool. O Allah! I ask You from Your Grace, Permissible, good, and I seek Refuge with You from being unjust and suffering injustice; and I seek Refuge with You from loss-making deals and false oaths'.

So when he says that, the Angel who is Allocated with him, says to him: 'Receive glad tidings! There is no one in your market which is more ampler than you in a share. The good has been hastened and the evil has been obliterated from you, and you will be receiving what Allah has Apportioned for you with ampleness, Permissible, good, with Blessings therein'.

key_terms.خَيْرِهَا وَ خَيْرِ أَهْلِهَا: Its goodness and the goodness of its people

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for entering and sitting in a marketplace according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) provides a structured spiritual protocol for navigating the commercial world, emphasizing that mindful remembrance transforms mundane transactions into acts of worship. It highlights the Shia emphasis on integrating faith into daily economic activities, promising angelic guardianship and the expiation of sins through specific invocations of divine favor and protection from deceit.
